docs/how-forge-works.html.tool-flow: export + checkTools{{tools}} registered tools ({{auto}} auto + {{onDemand}} on demand), as defined by packages/mcp-server/src/tools/registry.json: compose, validate, render, code, charts, dashboards, certify, tokens, catalog.
docs/how-forge-works.html.trait-format: A trait file has a named header (trait:). Across the authored inventory, its {{traitSectionCount}} section names are {{traitSectionRoster}}; each trait uses the sections it needs. The table below explains the core sections using Stateful as the example:
docs/how-forge-works.html.trait-states: From that, Product gains a status field restricted to those {{productStateCount}} values, a transition history, and a computed list of next states; every Product list shows a status badge, every detail page a status timeline, every form a status selector whose options come from the object's own states. Parameters flow into component props (optionsParameter: states), so the same StatusSelector is correct for Product's {{productStateCount}} states and Subscription's {{subscriptionStateCount}}. Parameter values are checked against each trait's JSON Schema (schemas/traits/<name>.parameters.schema.json) when the full engine resolves an object — pnpm object:validate, object:compose, object:generate; the tools' lighter composer merges without validating, so run object:validate after editing an object.
docs/how-forge-works.html.domain-traits: The {{domainTraitsWord}} SaaS-billing traits live in a domain pack (domains/saas-billing/) — a folder of traits and objects for one vertical that the engine loads alongside the core set. That is the mechanism for adding a new domain without touching core traits.
docs/how-forge-works.html.product-fields: • Fields are merged — every trait's schema fields plus the object's own: {{productFields}} fields for Product. If two traits declare the same field, the full engine applies collision rules (same type → merge, keep the stricter; two enums → union; required beats optional; different types → error unless the object resolves it) and records which trait each field came from.
docs/how-forge-works.html.product-parameter-type: • Parameters are applied — validated against each trait's schema, and parameter-driven enums become real constraints (Product's generated TypeScript type has status: {{productStatesType}}).
docs/how-forge-works.html.composer-semantics: The full engine (src/core, src/registry; the object:* commands) performs the composition steps above. The tools' runtime composer (packages/mcp-server; what object show and design.compose use) merges schema, semantics, view extensions and tokens only — last-wins on collisions with a warning, no parameter validation — and orders extensions higher-priority-first (default {{runtimePriority}}), where the React view engine orders lower-first (default {{viewPriority}}).
docs/how-forge-works.html.object-title: 05The object inventory ({{objectDefinitions}} definitions; {{objectNames}} unique names)
docs/how-forge-works.html.object-homes: The {{objectDefinitions}} definitions include Subscription in two homes. The saas-billing pack also defines its own Subscription (Stripe/Chargebee-shaped, with metering); because objects/ is scanned before domains/, the tools expose the core Subscription under that name. Adding an object is a new *.object.yaml file (the suffix is required) in objects/ or a domain pack; the loaders index once per process, so it appears on the next server start.
docs/how-forge-works.html.context-roster:
Context

The kind of screen an object is being shown in. A trait's view extension names the context it targets, so the same object produces a different — but consistent — screen for each. Traits contribute to list, detail, form, timeline, card and inline. Bound bar and line traits also author dashboard contributions, selected through the public dashboard layout. The chart view remains a shell.
docs/how-forge-works.html.region-roster: Every context in Forge's component library is laid out on the same {{regionsWord}} named regions, in this order: {{regionRoster}}. Main is always required; page header is required in every context except card and inline; list and timeline also require the toolbar. Regions render as real HTML landmarks (nav, header, main, aside with labels), so structure is visible to screen readers and testable.
docs/how-forge-works.html.view-assembly: How a screen is assembled. For the requested context, Forge collects every trait's extensions, sorts them by priority (lower first, default {{viewPriority}}; ties by declaration order), evaluates any conditions (data, permissions, theme), groups them by region and composes them in a fixed order. Each rendered piece is wrapped in a boundary carrying its id, region and source trait, and a debug mode prints a per-region report. Below tablet width ({{tabletWidth}}px container) the two-column contexts collapse to one column; an opt-in drawer component turns the side panel into a focus-trapped sheet.
docs/how-forge-works.html.renderer-layouts: There are two renderers. The React view engine (the component library, Storybook, the region contract above) and the tools' HTML renderer, which places the same trait contributions into layout templates — {{renderLayouts}} — with named slots (header, tab-N, metadata, items, filters, hero, cta …). Generated HTML documents carry the tokens and components, not yet the {{regionsWord}}-region responsive shell.
docs/how-forge-works.html.component-counts: The canonical intake contains {{components}} unique component claims. The historical reconciliation proposal classified {{historicalRuntime}} as runtime component rows ({{historicalNative}} native and {{historicalRecipes}} recipes) and {{historicalAuthoring}} as non-runtime authoring-only rows. Derek accepted retaining all 109 obligations in decision #1788; Sprint 199 adds VizGraphPreview as the 110th obligation under decision #2054; the old {{historicalRuntime}}-runtime split remains unapproved and approvedRuntimeCensus stays null. Missing implementations remain obligations. Sprint-182 evidence marks exactly {{foundationReact}} React and {{foundationVue}} Vue surface cells as foundation-v1-candidate; a separate independent review accepted those candidates and a distinct authorization promoted all {{foundationPromoted}} to foundation-v1. That promotion does not approve the {{historicalRuntime}}-row runtime census. That historical foundation nucleus is {{foundationRoster}}. The current evidence measures {{reactComponents}} React and {{vueComponents}} Vue implementations, {{htmlComponents}} HTML mappings, and {{contracts}} versioned contracts. Accessibility is verified for {{accessibleComponents}} rows and theme for {{themedComponents}} rows; interaction is verified for {{interactiveComponents}} and explicitly not applicable for {{staticComponents}} static rows. No framework row is unavailable. These are measured component scenarios and bounded runtime receipts; Sprint 193 is certified and closed. The authored shared scenario roster contains {{scenarios}} scenarios. The generated capability ledger and date-tagged catalog export agree. The current proposal is {{nativeComponents}} native, {{recipeComponents}} recipe and {{aliasComponents}} alias; all {{components}} classifications await Derek’s approval; the independent Sprint 192 review certified the sprint (decision #1891) without approving the proposal. catalog.list filters the catalog by category, trait or context; object show returns an object's composed traits and extensions.
docs/how-forge-works.html.token-outputs: One build (pnpm build:tokens, Style Dictionary) compiles the JSON sources into {{tokenOutputs}} outputs: CSS custom properties ({{tokenVariables}} variables), a TypeScript map, a Tailwind token map, a Swift file and a Kotlin file. Tokens are layered so that a change at the right level propagates:
docs/how-forge-works.html.token-themes: Themes are light, dark and high-contrast (the last maps to the operating system's forced colours). Brands are sets of values for the brand colour roles — surfaces, text, interactive, borders, status and focus — one JSON file per brand per theme (the base files contain {{tokenLeaves}} leaves each, under brands/<X>/{base,dark,hc}.json). The build emits a block per brand × theme that re-assigns {{bridgedSlots}} shared theme slots to that brand's values:
docs/how-forge-works.html.token-brands: So switching brand or theme is two attributes on the document; no component changes. {{brandCountWord}} brands ship today ({{brandRoster}}); {{presetCountWord}} brand-relative presets ({{presetRoster}}) can be applied to any brand. brand.intake validates inline brand-relative DTCG documents and returns an envelope hash plus a consumable delta for accepted A/B themes. brand.apply previews that delta or writes canonical brand source and runs both token-build stages, retaining source hashes, byte counts and captured build results in a dated review folder. A failed build reports the output tail and leaves source writes in place. tokens.build returns requested-scope JSON and CSS alongside full CSS and legacy A/light TypeScript and Tailwind artifacts.
docs/how-forge-works.html.token-guards: Guards around the build. A collision guard refuses to build if two source files declare the same token with different values; {{brandContrastRules}} brand-contrast rules ({{brandContrastPairs}} text/icon pairs per brand per theme) run in CI, and any theme slot a brand newly overrides must be graded; a real-browser check asserts the computed values in all {{brandThemeCells}} brand × theme cells; a CI check blocks high-risk token changes (by namespace and segment) unless the PR carries the token-change:breaking label.
docs/how-forge-works.html.generation-path: The generate path is four stages that chain — compose, validate, render and generate — with pipeline running them together. They pass a UiSchema between them:
docs/how-forge-works.html.ui-schema-shape:
UiSchema

A JSON tree of components. The schema declares node properties {{uiNodeProperties}} and root properties {{uiRootProperties}}. Traits' token maps are carried into tokenOverrides.
docs/how-forge-works.html.compose-tool: design.composeA short intent ("order history list with filters") and/or an object + context ({{composeContexts}}), optional layout ({{composeLayouts}}) and component overrides.A UiSchema plus a reference id ({{ttlMinutes}}-minute lifetime), per-slot confidence, and a review hint where a slot was uncertain. Object-aware: it fills slots from the object's fields and view extensions and reports which traits it used.
docs/how-forge-works.html.validate-tool: repl · validateA UiSchema, or a patch to one (JSON Patch or per-node replace).Structural validation against the schema grammar and the component catalog; optionally the {{tokenContrastRules}} token-contrast rules.
docs/how-forge-works.html.codegen-tool: code.generateA validated UiSchema; framework {{frameworks}}; styling {{styling}}; TypeScript on/off.A single-screen schema returns source code plus its import list; a workflow returns application files. React imports the real @oods/components-react package, Vue imports @oods/components-vue, and both import @oods/component-styles/css. A known component/target pair that is not emission-eligible fails before emission with typed error OODS-N015 and no source payload; HTML remains standalone.
docs/how-forge-works.html.schema-lifetime: schema · save/load/list/deleteA schema reference.Persists work past the {{ttlMinutes}}-minute reference lifetime and across sessions.
docs/how-forge-works.html.product-screen: Intent matching is rule-based (keywords and synonyms choose the layout; a deterministic selector picks components), so the same input always produces the same tree — there is no language model inside Forge. A real run: intent "product detail page" auto-detects the Product object, picks the detail layout, and returns a {{productNodes}}-node tree with {{productSlots}} filled slots and {{productTabs}} tabs expanded from Product's {{productFields}} fields. The actual selected slot roster is {{productSlotRoster}}.
docs/how-forge-works.html.fidelity-and-datasets: Alongside: fidelity.preview renders an object manifest at {{fidelitiesWord}} fidelities (boxes-and-arrows, wireframe, review, branded mockup, using built A/B light tokens); deprecated brand-a/brand-b aliases remain for one release and unknown brands fail explicitly. map records and resolves mappings for external consumers; no composer or generator consumes them. Draft preferred terms and disambiguation decisions are surfaced, not consumed by resolution; structuredData.fetch serves the components and tokens datasets and registry.snapshot serves traits, objects and mappings, all versioned with ETags.
docs/how-forge-works.html.portable-outcomes: The portable adapter calls all {{portableTools}} advertised tools in the retained E2E. {{portablePass}} return the exercised result and {{portableTyped}} {{portableTypedPhrase}}: {{portableLimits}}. brand.apply previews from the shipped brand source and, with apply, emits its review kit without writing the bundle. The native code is preserved at tools/call. tokens.build executes from the shipped built artifacts; readiness attestations bind React/Vue generation to shipped package bytes. The separate extracted-bundle reference-app ledger records {{releaseCells}} cells across {{releaseApps}}, {{releaseContexts}} contexts in {{releaseFrameworks}}: {{releasePass}} pass, {{releaseTyped}} typed gaps, and {{releaseEqual}} generated artifacts equal the corresponding host hashes.
docs/how-forge-works.html.viz-taxonomy: The versioned taxonomy classifies {{taxonomyIdentities}} chart identities ({{taxonomyTypes}} types and {{taxonomyPatterns}} patterns) across {{taxonomyFamiliesWord}} families and records active Core Analytics Profile cells as surface-complete or typed gaps, with retired cells and their reasons recorded separately.
docs/how-forge-works.html.viz-vocabulary: viz.render takes data and returns a chart specification. {{chartTypesWord}} chart types: {{cartesianRoster}} (from tabular rows; compiled to Vega-Lite, ECharts on request) and {{primaryRoster}} (from node/link/geometry inputs; ECharts). Four input modes: a catalog pattern identity, explicit (chart type + encodings), suggest (rows only — the recommender picks), or a structured intent (goal, measures, dimensions). Pattern mode uses bundled authored data and presentation; scenes preserve layers, bounded facets and secondary axes, retired patterns return OODS-V174 with reasons, and unsupported data structures return OODS-V167, and conflicting explicit operands return OODS-V166. The {{cartesianCountWord}} Cartesian families return spec; the {{primaryCountWord}} ECharts-primary families omit spec and return echartsSpec with output.echarts forced true and reason echarts-primary-family. Every successful result carries a content hash of the canonical spec; on request it also returns an accessible data table and a generated narrative derived from the same data. The {{vizTraits}} viz-category traits (marks, encodings, scales, layouts, interactions, scatter composition and geocoding) are the vocabulary the spec is normalised into. Temporal axes and adapter-generated formatted date parsing use UTC, independent of the host timezone. Caller-authored expressions retain their own semantics. ScaleTemporal declares no timezone parameter; rendering uses UTC; numeric tooltips use en-US.
docs/how-forge-works.html.dashboard-vocabulary: dashboard.render composes a metric overview — KPI tiles, a trend panel, a breakdown panel, optional geo — from shared datasets and panel definitions, with deterministic auto-layout and cross-filter linking, and can export one self-contained HTML file with server-rendered SVG for its {{dashboardTypes}} admitted chart types in light and dark: Vega-Lite for the {{cartesianCountWord}} Cartesian families and ECharts for {{dashboardPrimaryWord}} primary families. Chord and flow_map remain excluded from the public dashboard panel schema (#881). Governed measureRef resolution defaults to true; unknown refs return OODS-V130 and missing fields return OODS-V137. Explicit resolveMeasures:false disables that resolution. Failed panels retain explicit error placeholders; a successful chart panel must have a renderable specification.
docs/how-forge-works.html.certify-pillars:
Certify

artifact.certify takes a chart specification back (and, for the advanced types, its data) and returns a per-check scorecard plus a combined conformance result on the declared certification path. Its {{certifyPillarsWord}} core certification pillars are accessibility equivalence, determinism, contrast and accuracy.
docs/how-forge-works.html.a11y-rule-count: Accessibility equivalence{{a11yRules}} structural rules over the chart and its text alternative: colour encodings carry a second cue and size differences are perceptible; an accessible table exists, captioned to the chart title, with declared column order; axis titles, an accessible name and a description at least {{a11yDescriptionMinimum}} characters are present; bar/stacked charts narrate extrema, trend charts narrate the trend, area charts describe their baseline/range; datasets with {{a11yFindingsRowMinimum}}+ rows surface at least {{a11yFindingsMinimumWord}} findings and dense ones aggregate; every encoded field is present in every row; the narrative generator reports ready; interactions describe their announcements. Each rule names its precondition; absent preconditions remain visible as not applicable. On the data-backed ECharts path, error-severity failures fail the accessibility pillar and conformance; warning-severity findings remain visible without failing the pillar.
docs/how-forge-works.html.determinism-scope: DeterminismTwo independent compiled or projected specifications are canonicalised and byte-compared, then independently rendered SVGs are compared. Content and render hashes identify the corresponding viz.render output for the same operand and scope; notes retain any rendering limitation and the certified runtime boundary.
docs/how-forge-works.html.contrast-thresholds: ContrastThe colour values actually baked into the spec are graded: every mark at least 3:1 against the requested light or dark theme canvas (WCAG 1.4.11); categorical palettes checked for distinguishability under normal vision and three colour-vision-deficiency simulations; gradient scales reported as exempt, not passed. The requested A/B brand and light/dark/hc theme are retained. High-contrast returns an exempt contrast result with reason forced-colors and no numeric grade; the browser resolves the declared system colours.
docs/how-forge-works.html.accuracy-rule-count: Accuracy{{accuracyRules}} reader-only structural-distortion rules: bar baseline not at zero (or on log/sqrt); dual y-axes in one frame; area on a non-linear scale; a row-merging aggregation not disclosed in title, description or axis; negative treemap/sunburst values; a parent not equal to the sum of its children; negative sankey/chord links; sankey node height inconsistent with its flows; duplicate sankey links; conflicting values joined to one map region; invalid bubble sizes and flow strengths, radius-based bubble scaling, duplicate geographic operands, and overlapping duplicate directed force-graph links. Reciprocal links remain distinct. "Pass" means no offered rule detected its distortion, and the count of rules that actually ran is reported. ECharts accuracy requires at least one evaluated rule; missing preconditions never count as a pass.
docs/how-forge-works.html.certify-scope: Coverage, stated plainly. The {{cartesianCountWord}} Cartesian types certify from their IR. Advanced types use the declared operand profile with the same data supplied to rendering: conformance requires accessibility to pass, contrast to be neither failed nor ungradeable, stable determinism, and evaluated-and-clean accuracy. Certified coverage can carry a measured false conformance result. Spec-only ECharts calls remain uncertified with null conformance and a missing-operand explanation; this path adds no Vega-Lite compile. Certification covers chart specs, not pages or components. It accepts brand A or B and theme light, dark or hc (defaults A/light), matching rendering and contrast grading. High-contrast SVG proof covers bar, line, area and scatter. Heatmap and the {{primaryCountWord}} ECharts types retain typed undeclared-paint failures; their render failure fails determinism and conformance. HC contrast alone is exempt with reason forced-colors. Forced-colours browser evidence covers chart SVGs, dashboard HTML and the React/Vue Subscription detail preview.
docs/how-forge-works.html.token-contrast: • Token contrast — a11y.scan (and repl validate on request) grades {{tokenContrastRules}} token pairs: primary text on canvas / raised / subtle surfaces, secondary, muted, accent and inverse text, the {{statusTextRules}} status text and {{statusIconRules}} status icon pairs, and {{darkContrastRules}} dark-theme primary-text variants — {{textContrastThreshold}}:1 for text, {{iconContrastThreshold}}:1 for icons.
docs/how-forge-works.html.browser-viewports: • Component library in CI — axe-core (WCAG 2.0 A + 2.1 AA, serious/critical) over a fixed set of Storybook stories in light and dark; Playwright behavioural checks at phone ({{phoneWidth}}), tablet ({{tabletWidth}}) and desktop widths (layout collapse, drawer focus trap, Escape to close, no violations with the drawer open); the brand-contrast and browser checks from section 07; optional Chromatic visual regression.
docs/how-forge-works.html.operating-roster: Start and connect. Build the server once: pnpm --filter @oods/mcp-server run build. Connect an AI assistant with the stdio adapter: docs/runtime/install.md carries the Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Cursor steps for the released runtime bundle, and configs/agents/ holds the same three generated config snippets for a clone. For a browser panel or HTTP-style agents, run the bridge (pnpm bridge:dev; it listens on 127.0.0.1:{{bridgePort}}). From the terminal, call any tool directly: pnpm exec tsx tools/oods-agent-cli/src/index.ts plan design.compose '{"intent":"product detail page"}'. The authoritative roster is packages/mcp-server/src/tools/registry.json: {{auto}} tools register by default and {{onDemand}} more switch on with MCP_TOOLSET=all.
docs/how-forge-works.html.safety-model: Safety model. Tools that write into the repo or artifacts (tokens.build, brand.apply, a11y.scan, billing.*, map.*, diag.snapshot, release.tag) preview by default and write only with apply: true; schema save persists on call and pipeline writes via its save option. {{rolesWord}} roles ({{roleRoster}} — release tools are maintainer-only); per-tool rate limits, concurrency and timeouts from a policy file; outputs land under artifacts/current-state/<date>/ with redacted transcripts and a hashed bundle index. Optional OpenTelemetry tracing per tool call.
docs/how-forge-works.html.generation-targets: • Generated HTML documents use the tokens and components but not the {{regionsWord}}-region responsive shell; code generation targets React, Vue and HTML only.
docs/how-forge-works.html.native-token-scope: • Typography shares global sans and display font stacks. The categorical chart palette resolves by brand and theme and accepts explicit token overrides. The Swift/Kotlin files carry one default brand × theme and omit font stacks and easing curves.
docs/how-forge-works.html.footer: Figures are generated from the Forge repository ({{traits}} traits · {{objectDefinitions}} object definitions / {{objectNames}} unique names · {{components}} governed component claims · {{contexts}} contexts · {{chartTypes}} chart types). The {{tools}}-tool roster comes from packages/mcp-server/src/tools/registry.json; contracts: packages/mcp-server/src/schemas/ and docs/api/.
docs/how-forge-works.html.state-machine-cardinality: • Tokens, semantics, actions and a state machine (multiple owners are refused by default) are merged.

docs/how-forge-works.html.release-evidence-limit: health reports built token scopes and a labelled configured defaultScope, not an observed consumer scope. design.preview requires the local design-loop server at 127.0.0.1:4477; otherwise it returns OODS-N019. Release-profile receipts from code.generate and pipeline carry evidenceVerification: hash-bound-not-re-executed. {{releaseEvidenceLimit}} Request dslVersion and repl.output.depth were removed because no handler consumed them; UiSchema.version remains.
docs/how-forge-works.html.object-chart-runtime-limit: Charts inside generated objects. Subscription keeps its payment-area chart in detail. Invoice declares a bar chart over line_items, preserving minor currency units and summing matching descriptions. Usage declares a temporal line chart over samples; its generated examples are explicitly synthetic API-call counts, consistent with the object's api_calls unit. Invoice and Usage author detail and dashboard placements. Trait title and description parameters travel with the chart. React and Vue application generation and HTML chart-node generation use actual renderer SVG; Static HTML tab panel trees preserve nested content and layout. Full Invoice/Usage detail HTML remains a typed OODS-V007 static-action limit: HTML has no runtime for domain actions such as Edit/Delete/View timeline. These passive sample assets stay fixed when a local record is edited, and consumers can supply a replacement SVG. The capability inventory observes composed declarations; generated-application runtime proof is recorded separately. Relationship declares a force graph in detail and workflow through MarkGraph and VizGraphPreview. Its optional neighborhood array is labelled Example connected relationships and contains explicitly synthetic edges. The edge-array transformation sorts distinct node IDs, retains source-to-target row order, adds a reverse link only for a true bidirectional flag, and deduplicates directed pairs without inventing weights or groups. The named wrapper preserves the native ECharts SVG. This ungrouped example has no categorical semantic metadata: light/dark contrast is ungradeable even though accuracy and determinism pass; HC contrast is exempt. Browser proof checks visible marks and labels in every scope. The inventory observes 10 declarations across 4 chart types. The other seven ECharts types remain unplaced: treemap and sunburst need hierarchy arrays; sankey and chord need numeric link values; choropleth, bubble_map and flow_map need inline geometry and their corresponding region, point or flow values.

docs/README.md.token-architecture:
### 1. Four-Layer Token Architecture (conceptual)

This diagram illustrates four design roles. It is not a count of implemented token namespaces; the modifier layer is a conceptual role.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Modifiers Layer (--mod-*)          │  ← Runtime variants (hover, focus, disabled)
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Component Layer (--cmp-*)          │  ← Component-specific tokens
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Theme Layer (--theme-*)            │  ← Light/dark, brand overlays
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Reference Layer (--ref-*)          │  ← Foundational design tokens
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The illustration recommends component-level aliases. The current build also includes system tokens; component implementations may reference those shared roles directly.

**→ [4-Layer Architecture Details](tokens/4-layer-overview.md)**
docs/README.md.quintet-example:
### Universal Quintet Pattern
The original modeling guide groups these examples into a “Universal Quintet.” This is a design vocabulary, not a measured prevalence claim:

1. **User/Person**: Authentication, authorization, identity
2. **Product/Item**: The "things" your system manages
3. **Transaction/Event**: State changes, business events
4. **Organization/Location**: Structural, spatial context
5. **Relationship/Association**: Many-to-many connections

**→ [Universal Quintet Reference](universal-quintet.md)**

README.md.schema-ttl: - `schemaRef` TTL: refs returned by `design.compose`, `design.preview`, `pipeline`, and `schema.load` last {{ttlMinutes}} minutes inside the server process that issued them; a client keeps that process for one conversation, and a restarted client starts a new one that does not know earlier refs (`OODS-N003`). README.md.what-forge-is:
OODS Forge is a design-system engine that an AI assistant drives over MCP. You name a screen by its object and its context; Forge composes the screen from governed components and tokens, generates it as React, Vue or HTML, renders charts and dashboards from your data, and certifies what it produced against accuracy, accessibility, contrast and determinism rules. It ships as a runtime bundle you extract and connect to Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor.

Today it knows {{objectNames}} objects, {{traits}} traits and {{components}} governed components, renders {{chartTypes}} chart types under a taxonomy of {{taxonomyPatterns}} named patterns, and advertises {{auto}} tools by default ({{tools}} in all).
README.md.three-words:
- **Object**: a thing your product has, described once with its fields and behaviours. `Subscription` is an object: a plan, a status, a billing interval and a payment history. Forge ships {{objectNames}} objects, each defined in YAML; you add your own the same way.
- **Trait**: a capability an object composes in, bringing its fields, states and screen contributions with it. `Subscription` composes `Stateful` (a status with allowed transitions) and `Billable`; `User` and `Organization` compose `Addressable`. There are {{traits}} traits, {{vizTraits}} of them chart traits.
- **Context**: the kind of screen an object is shown in. The same `Subscription` produces a different but consistent screen for each of {{composeContexts}}; a trait's view extension says what it contributes to which context.
README.md.generates-and-certifies:
Forge generates React, Vue and HTML screens and whole workflow applications from composed screens, with every component drawn from the {{components}} governed components and every colour, space and type value from the token system. {{brandCountWord}} brands ship today, each with light, dark and high-contrast themes. It renders {{chartTypes}} chart types from your data ({{cartesianRoster}} from tabular rows; {{primaryRoster}} from node, link and geometry inputs) and composes dashboards of KPI tiles, trend, breakdown and map panels over {{dashboardTypes}} admitted chart types, as tokened SVG and specs.

"Certify" is a measurement, not a promise. `artifact.certify` takes a chart specification Forge rendered and runs its {{certifyPillarsWord}} pillars on it: accuracy ({{accuracyRules}} structural-distortion rules about baselines, hidden aggregation, mis-scaled encodings and inconsistent structure; a chart is graded on the ones that apply to its type, and the result names them), accessibility equivalence (the narrative and the data table say what the chart says), contrast (the drawn paints against the tokens) and determinism (two independent renders hash the same). Each pillar reports pass or fail with findings, and `coverage` says whether the chart type is on the certified path. Generated screens carry a `validationReceipt` from `code.generate` naming the checks that ran (schema structure, component registry, state contract, target readiness, dependency closure and more) and, under `notChecked`, the ones that did not. No receipt claims a check it did not run.
README.md.first-run-health: The default surface is {{auto}} tools; `MCP_TOOLSET=all` advertises all {{tools}}, and `health` reports the counts it serves.

# @oods/mcp-server

Native tool handlers for OODS Forge. Build from the repository root with `pnpm --filter @oods/mcp-server run build`; start with `pnpm --filter @oods/mcp-server start`. MCP clients normally use the [stdio adapter](../mcp-adapter/) or [HTTP bridge](../mcp-bridge/).

The registry advertises {{auto}} tools by default and {{onDemand}} on demand ({{tools}} total). Enable on-demand entries with `MCP_TOOLSET=all` or select them with `MCP_EXTRA_TOOLS`.

The retained portable adapter E2E exercises {{portableTools}} advertised tools: {{portablePass}} results and {{portableTyped}} typed dependency {{portableLimitNoun}}, {{portableLimits}}. Source evidence tiers below do not imply executed proof for every tool.

Retired tools and their rationale are recorded in the generated [Tool-Specs retirement table](../../docs/mcp/Tool-Specs.md).

The extracted-bundle reference-app ledger records {{releaseCells}} cells for {{releaseApps}} across {{releaseContexts}} contexts and {{releaseFrameworks}}: {{releasePass}} pass, {{releaseTyped}} typed gaps and {{releaseEqual}} generated artifacts equal their host hashes. These bounded receipts do not imply universal application coverage.

Extracted distribution: [portable runtime](../../docs/runtime/portable-runtime.md).

Generation targets {{frameworks}}. References expire after {{ttlMinutes}} minutes unless persisted through `schema` (`action: save`). React and Vue readiness attestations verify shipped package hashes without shipping source/tests; mismatches refuse generation with OODS-N015.

# @oods/mcp-bridge

HTTP transport for the native Forge server. Build the server first, then run `pnpm --filter @oods/mcp-bridge run dev` from the repository root. The extracted portable runtime also includes this bridge and its policies.

The default listener is `127.0.0.1:{{bridgePort}}`; `MCP_BRIDGE_PORT` overrides the port. `BRIDGE_TOKEN` enables the `X-Bridge-Token` header. Write-gated calls use `X-Bridge-Approval` according to policy. Endpoints are `GET /health`, `GET /tools`, `POST /run` and `/artifacts/*`; refresh `/tools` for the live enabled surface. Build revision and availability are reported by health.
